summary: The core event is the Sir Ivan Fire, ignited by lightning near Leadville on 11 February 2017 and driven by catastrophic fire-danger conditions the next day; it burned roughly 55,000 hectares through Warrumbungle Shire (Uarbry, Leadville, Cassilis, Coolah, Dunedoo), destroying 31-35 homes (figures vary by assessment stage), a church and a community hall, well over 100 outbuildings, and killing thousands of livestock (2,000 sheep, 56 cattle, 90 goats and others). The same catastrophic weekend produced related fires assessed together by NSW RFS: the Pappinbarra fire in Port Macquarie-Hastings LGA (6 homes destroyed) and the Spring Hill Road, Dondingalong fire in Kempsey LGA (2 homes destroyed), plus the White Cedars Rd fire spilling into Mid-Western Regional. Total confirmed home losses across this fire cluster reached 41 by the RFS's 15 February bulletin, though this total also includes an unrelated Boggabri (Narrabri LGA) fire outside the 6 listed councils. This declaration's council list also includes two August 2017 fires (Parrabel Creek, Carrolls Creek per the seed dataset) that may belong to a separate later NDRRA activation for Kempsey/Mid-Coast/Port Macquarie-Hastings -- unresolved. Recovery efforts, including a reported $1 million BlazeAid fencing fund, continued for many months afterward.

summary: The Carwoola bushfire ignited on 17 February 2017 near Queanbeyan on a catastrophic fire-danger, Total Fire Ban day and burned over 3,500 hectares through the weekend. It destroyed 11 homes and 45 outbuildings, damaged a further 12 homes and 40 outbuildings, and injured two firefighters (no deaths reported). Evacuation centres were set up at the Q Theatre in Queanbeyan and Bungendore Public School hall. Two men were later charged over allegedly starting the fire.
